pages.text: A society begins when a culture's people take root in the right climate. Only the $(thing)newcomer$(0) class arrives on its own; every other class is reached by rising through the ladder. Meet their basic needs and they will settle and, in time, have children.$(br2)Elites and leaders never have children of their own. They are $(thing)made, not born$(0): your settlement must keep raising them from below.

Citizens also $(thing)work$(0). Each class entry lists its jobs and the building each one needs, so a farmer wants a farm, a miller a mill, a guard a weapon. Build the workplaces before you hope to see the jobs filled, and plan your quarter around them.$(br2)Think at $(thing)city scale$(0): dozens to a couple of hundred citizens, with many modest homes and a handful of impressive shared buildings.

Each culture's officiants hold $(thing)rites$(0): gatherings in a hall, shrine or plaza that citizens want held nearby. A rite consumes offerings that you supply, and the offerings are listed on the culture's overview. The bigger your settlement, the more rites you will want held, and the more you will need to produce.
